title: Sporadic dimension mismatch — deep dive and quick repros
content:
Summary:
- Intermittent failures from rerank service complaining about embedding vector length: 'INVALID_VECTOR_DIM: expected 1536, got 1535'.
- Failure rate ~0.25–0.8% of requests over last 10 days. Correlates with latency spikes (p95 up to 600ms) and a rolling deploy on 2026-03-02.

Quick repro (minimal):
1) Request an embedding from hosted embeddings endpoint (model: open-embed-large-v1)
$ curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-large-v1","input":"test repro string"}' | jq .

Expected: json with "embedding": [1536 floats]
Observed failing case (example):
{
  "error": "INVALID_VECTOR_DIM",
  "message": "expected 1536, got 1535"
}

2) Send returned vector to rerank endpoint (server-side) -> immediate validation error.

Local quick harness (python):
- send N embeddings and count failures; reproduces ~1/300 locally if routed to affected nodes.

snippet:
import requests
for i in range(1000):
    r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={'model':'open-embed-large-v1','input':'foo %d'%i}, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer '+TOKEN})
    emb = r.json().get('embedding')
    if emb and len(emb) != 1536:
        print('bad len', len(emb), 'i', i)
        break

What I inspected so far:
- Model selection: only open-embed-large-v1 in repros. Quantization/compilation looks consistent.
- Affected vectors always appear to be missing exactly 1 float at the tail (1535 instead of 1536). Never >1 missing, never extra.
- Failures spike for requests routed to a particular worker pool (eu-west-1 pool-3).
- Disk/storage: embeddings are ephemeral (returned by model process), not read from DB; suggests serialization/transport bug.
- Timestamps: first uptick on 2026-03-03 03:14 UTC (right after rolling deploy, which touched the embeddings transport layer).

Relevant log snippets (from worker):
[2026-03-03T03:14:02Z] WARN serialize_vector: truncated buf length 6143 -> expected 6144 (float32)
[2026-03-03T03:14:02Z] ERROR api: validate_vector_len failed: expected 1536 got 1535 (req_id=abc123)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Byte-level serialization bug in C++ transport wrapper when using non-zero-length metadata header: off-by-one when computing total bytes (most likely).
2) Race between streaming response chunking and finalization hook: last float occasionally dropped when a tiny trailing chunk boundary occurs.
3) Client HTTP library in older nodes occasionally trims a trailing "\n" or null byte causing decoder to parse one fewer float.
4) Model runtime emitting 1536 floats but last element is NaN and a filter step drops NaNs (rare).
5) Post-quantization compaction removing trailing zero when compression enabled.

Commands/traces I ran:
- grep the worker logs for 'truncated buf length' across clusters:
$ rg "truncated buf length" /var/log/embeddings/* | sort -r
- tcpdump of request between model-runtime and transport on affected worker (PCAP showed final 4 bytes absent in reproductions).
- Added an assert in the transport serializer to verify bytes_written == expected_bytes and logged stack trace when not equal.

Quick mitigation patch (deployed to routing layer 2026-03-05):
- client-side: validate vector length before calling rerank; if shorter, pad with 0.0 to 1536 and attach 'padded=true' to metadata.
- server-side: rerank accepts padded vectors (temporary) but emits metric rerank.padded_count.
Effect: reduced customer-facing errors to 0.0%, but masked root cause; metric shows ~0.3% padded.

Experiments and results:
- Increased request chunk size on transport to avoid split-chunk boundary: reduced failures by ~70%.
- Switched to non-chunked (Content-Length) on affected nodes -> failures stopped for that subset. Suggests chunking boundary bug.
- Recompiling transport with -fsanitize=address not helpful for small memory write issues; race remains intermittent.

What I still need to do / TODOs:
- [ ] Reproduce locally without routing (attempt to trigger chunk boundary with deliberate small MTU simulation).
- [ ] Add deterministic unit test simulating chunked writes with off-by-one size.
- [ ] Code review C++ serializer: look for write() call that subtracts 1 from total length incorrectly. Suspect code in src/transport/writer.cc line ~128 (TODO get exact).
- [ ] Run long-run harness against eu-west-1 pool-3 with debug logs enabled (low-rate to avoid customer impact).
- [ ] Rollback partial chunking optimization landed 2026-03-02 if reproduction continues.

Quick repro script idea (to run in dev account):
1) Start a minimal mock server that emits a vector as binary float32 with deliberately chunked Transfer-Encoding: chunked output, vary chunk sizes and boundary offsets.
2) Run our transport client against it and assert length.
3) Iterate until client sees missing 4 bytes.

Notes & oddities: 
- The missing float is always the last element, and the last 4-byte read fails only when chunk boundary aligns exactly after 6140 bytes (i.e., not multiples of 4). That smells like an off-by-byte arithmetic error converting floats->bytes in header calc.
- Some affected nodes are on slightly older glibc (2.28) vs others (2.31) — differences in write() buffering behavior could amplify the race.
- No evidence yet of model-side truncation (model runtime logs show 1536 floats produced).

Follow-ups for other teams:
- Serving-runtime: add temporary validation on model outputs before serialization and log if count != expected. (ticket INF-4721 assigned).
- Platform/infra: flag eu-west-1 pool-3 nodes and consider draining if we can't reproduce quickly.
- SDKs: keep client-side padding for 24–72h as protection and ship a small warning in logs for any padded vectors.

Notes for when this regresses:
- Check metric 'embeddings.padded_count' and correlate with rerank.errors.
- grep for 'serialize_vector: truncated' and track req_ids for full traces.

Benchmarks/latency correlation:
- Baseline p95 embeddings time pre-deploy: ~110ms. After deploy: baseline stable, but p95 for failing nodes spikes to ~420–600ms during window when chunk boundary causes retry/extra processing.
- p50 unaffected.

Immediate contact list:
- Maya Patel (applied-ml) - oncall for embeddings this week
- Luca Moretti (serving-runtime) - transport owner
- Priya Singh (platform) - infra/drain plan

Conclusion:
Evidence strongly points to a chunking/serialization off-by-one in transport on a subset of nodes after the 2026-03-02 deploy. Short-term mitigation (pad-on-client) is in place; next steps are deterministic repro, targeted insert of extra asserts/logging in serializer, and either rolling back chunking or patching the write-size calc.

Appendix - sample failing curl output (raw):
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "INVALID_VECTOR_DIM",
    "message": "expected 1536, got 1535"
  },
  "req_id": "abc123"
}

If anyone picks this up: start with a small reproduce harness that forces chunk sizes 1..32 and try to find a deterministic pattern. If you need access to eu-west-1 pool-3 logs, ping me and I'll share the temporary S3 link.

-- Evan
